sourceAuthorityJustification.adoptedInference: For this supported scope, satisfy dispositive-order procedure with court-issued post-decision receipt/follow-up rather than a generated applicant proposed order. procedure.participantInstrument: CRM-307 petition; participant signs and completes actual service requirements. Existing prosecutor-response/hearing regions remain reserved to their proper actors.
procedure.draftingActor: Unspecified in source; do not invent clerk/applicant preparer.
procedure.postDecisionReceipt: After grant obtain actual issued order copy; record its genuine date and identifiers only when present. Pending/denied cases carry no synthetic granted order.

distribution.uponIssuance: Court supplies order copies to defendant and prosecuting attorney.
distribution.within30Days: Court forwards copies to arresting/participating law-enforcement agencies and master local criminal-history agency.
distribution.departmentOfJustice: Court furnishes disposition report identifying relief statute/date; does not forward sealing order for DOJ criminal-history processing under851.92(b)(1)(C)-(D).

requiredParticipantComponents: Existing completion proof supplied by participant as required

procedure.noticeAndHearing: Preserve notice to all parties, required prosecutor service, conditional hearing and law-enforcement notice branch. Prosecutor service is not every possible notice obligation.
procedure.protectedControls: All CRM307 prosecutor-response and court-notice decisions, signatures and dates remain protected. Participant optional appearance waiver is never automatically selected.
procedure.specificCourtRequest: A specific receiving-court request for a proposed order or additional submission controls. Surface it for supported completion or assistance; never fabricate the requested instrument.
procedure.statusTruth: Filing, successful completion and lack of opposition do not establish sealing. Obtain and retain the genuine issued decision document after the decision; it is not an initial-render prerequisite.
